text: 🏭 Mexico opens a public call to build Olinia — majority Mexican capital required. "The goal is very clear: a solid company, with majority Mexican capital, able to produce these vehicles in our country." — Rosaura Ruiz, Secretary of Science (Secihti) With Nacional Financiera, the government will launch a public, competitive call to select strategic manufacturing partners. National and foreign companies compete on equal terms — rules public from day one.

🔌 Plugs into any outlet. Costs 4x less to run than a cargo van. "Operating Olinia costs four times less than a light cargo vehicle — and a third of what it costs to operate a motocarro." — Roberto Capuano, Olinia project director A new category is born: compact electric minivehicles for local, low-speed trips. Not motorcycles, not cars. The Economy Secretariat is building regulatory certainty for the segment.
banner: OLINIA: 4X CHEAPER TO RUN THAN A VAN

text: 🛻 650 kg payload, 120+ km range, 12 crates. Price: around 150,000 pesos. "Today we show you — and Mexico — Olinia Carga: the minicar that carries big." — Roberto Capuano, Olinia project director Fits 12 huacales — Mexico's standard produce crates — with drop-side panels on all sides and a lower trunk where a gas engine would sit. Olinia 1 goes on sale summer 2027; Carga, late 2027.

🚗⚡ Olinia Carga: Mexico's second homegrown mini-EV, unveiled at the National Palace. "The goal is to promote mini-electromobility in our country — vehicles designed for the characteristics of Mexico, with the best engineering developed by public universities." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting Olinia Carga 70 engineers and specialists from TecNM, IPN, UNAM and state universities develop Olinia in Puebla. Today: the cargo model — and the plan to turn the project into a company through mixed public-private investment.

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICO'S ECONOMY: +2.7% ANNUAL IN JULY</u>

No recession here. INEGI's IOAE nowcast has Mexico's economy growing 2.7% annually in July, accelerating from 2.0% in June, with both industry and services expanding, El Economista reports. Monthly growth was a modest 0.1% — on top of a 1.5% quarterly GDP expansion in Q2, in the middle of Washington's tariff war. Private analysts keep forecasting 1.2% for 2026; the economy keeps beating their obituaries.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICO CITY'S ARTISTS: ONE MINUTE AGAINST GENOCIDE</u>

Mexico's cultural heavyweights filled the Teatro Esperanza Iris for "Un Minuto Contra el Genocidio": Paco Ignacio Taibo II in the hall, Elena Poniatowska by video, El Fisgón and Luisa Huertas on stage, messages from Demian Bichir, Laura Restrepo and Sergio Arau. Convened by the Liga Cultural Antifascista, their demand was blunt — an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Neutrality, they insisted, is unacceptable.

🇲🇽🫂 <u>CDMX: THE RIGHT TO CARE GOES CONSTITUTIONAL</u>

Mexico City is writing care into its legal DNA. Mayor Clara Brugada is pushing constitutional recognition of new rights — care, arraigo, early education and guaranteed income from age three — while the capital's human rights commission (CDHCDMX) sets up multi-actor working groups on the right to the city and the right to care. "May caring stop being a destiny imposed on women," Brugada said, "and may we advance toward eradicating the sexual division of labor."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>PUBLIC HEALTH: SPECIALTY CONSULTS UP 60% SINCE 2022</u>

Mexico's public health system delivered 31.7 million specialty consultations in January–July 2026, up from 19.7 million in the same period of 2022 — a 60% jump across IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS-Bienestar. Growth was sharpest where the federal model arrived: +90% in the 24 states federalized into IMSS-Bienestar, versus 20% in those that haven't joined. "Is the public health system doing better? Yes — it's a great indicator," Sheinbaum said.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>35,500 WELFARE HOMES DELIVERED — AND COUNTING</u>

Infonavit has placed 35,500 Vivienda para el Bienestar homes in 114 developments across Mexico, on the road to 1.8 million this sexenio. The latest delivery: 88 families received their keys in Tlaxcala, a state with a 10,000-home goal. Decades of neoliberal policy turned housing into an asset class; the 4T is turning it back into a right.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO THE DEA: PICK A LANE</u>

President Sheinbaum called out Washington's double discourse on security: DEA chief Terry Cole publicly praised Omar García Harfuch as a trusted US ally at the IDEC conference in Buenos Aires — while his agency keeps recycling evidence-free insinuations of cartel "links" to the Mexican state. "They recognize the work of García Harfuch, but then they allude to supposed ties," she said. Mexico coordinates. It doesn't take dictation.
